summary.headline: Bhagyanagar India crossed ₹2,000 crore revenue and ₹50 crore PAT in FY26; Q4 revenue ₹735 crore, PAT ₹18.5 crore, EBITDA margin ~5%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 as a record year: revenue above ₹2,000 crore, operational EBITDA above ₹100 crore and PAT above ₹50 crore for the first time. Q4 was the best quarter of the year, with revenue of about ₹735 crore, EBITDA of about ₹36 crore and PAT of about ₹18.5 crore. Volumes rose about 34% to 24,000 tonnes, and value-added share reached about 62% by Q4 (from 52% in Q1). Management guided to roughly 5% EBITDA margin, 20% volume growth and a 25% revenue CAGR, and said the demerger into copper and real estate verticals awaits NCLT hearing on 9 June.

financial_highlights.value: About ₹36 crore EBITDA; about ₹18.5 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PAT margin ~2.5% in Q4 (2.2% in Q3)

financial_highlights.value: About ₹43 for FY26; about ₹62 in Q4

financial_highlights.change: From ₹207 crore; increase via retained earnings, no dilution
From ₹157 crore; management says proportional to revenue

segments.name: Copper value-added products
segments.commentary: Value-added share was about 62% at end of Q4 versus 52% in Q1, with a target of 66% by end of FY27. Silver- and tin-plated bus bars for data centres are new, with exports to Canada and US; management expects them to reach 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years and about 10% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Copper recycling (backward integration)
segments.commentary: Capacity reached 35,000 tonnes this year (up from 30,000 in March 2026). Scrap sourcing from the Gulf is under 5% of input; US is the largest single source at 35%.

segments.name: Plastic and aluminium recycling (planned)
segments.commentary: Plan to invest about ₹10 crore in plastic recycling, processing cable-linked plastic into granules and aluminium into ingots; management targets 12-15 month payback. Revenue contribution expected to be small.

segments.name: Real estate (land parcels)
segments.commentary: Book value of real estate about ₹29 crore; three parcels (Nacharam ~4 acres, Upal ~4.5 acres, Hardware Park ~5 acres). Only Upal is under active consideration for development or joint development.

guidance_outlook: Maintain ~5% EBITDA margin through FY27 on a higher top line; management said 4.5-5% is a good margin for this business.
Target revenue of ₹5,000 crore for the copper company in about 3 years (around 2030), i.e. a 20-25% CAGR; the 25% growth expectation for next year is split as ~20% volume and ~5% price.
Q1 FY27: volume marginally below Q4 but well above Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 revenue about ₹486 crore); EBITDA margin expected to hold near 5%.
Planned capex of about ₹40 crore over the next two years, including the ₹10 crore plastic recycling project.
Fundraise of about ₹150 crore being considered; no final modality yet; management hopes to execute in FY27.
Working capital days expected to fall 2-3 days over the year.
capex_capacity: Copper capacity at 35,000 tonnes after increase from 30,000 tonnes in March 2026, in the new 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.
Heat recovery systems on furnaces to improve fuel efficiency and cut cycle times, going live in FY27.
About ₹40 crore capex over the next two years on capacities and new ventures; ₹10 crore for plastic recycling, to be scaled up over the next year.
Plastic recycling capacity plan reportedly from 150 to 500 (management confirmed intent to increase, sourcing only cable-linked plastic).
demand_pricing: Management expects copper consumption growth driven by EV/auto, power electrification and renewables; said India could become the second-largest copper consumer.
Pass-through of copper price to finished products is in place; additional margin pass-on is not assured and needs more value-added mix.
Management sees primary copper shortage in 3-4 years, with recycled copper filling the gap; no shortage expected for 2-3 years.

Copper price: FY26 realisation about ₹963 per kg per an analyst's figure; current copper price cited at about ₹1,300 per kg by an analyst; management assumed about 5% annual copper price rise for guidance.
Scrap availability: Gulf-origin scrap dried up due to shipping transshipment disruption; management says BIL is less affected than the industry because Gulf exposure is under 5%.
Competition: Adani and Hindalco entering recycling; management believes sourcing relationships and 40-year history provide an edge.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 growth was about 35% volume and 10% price; FY27 target is about 20% volume and 5% price, with 15-20% minimum volume growth each year.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity size and margins for silver/tin bus bars?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% EBITDA margin; contribution still very small, expected 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years with slow ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Is copper scrap availability a concern after the Gulf disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry is affected more than BIL; Gulf is under 5% of BIL's input and US is 35%. Management expects normalisation as shipping resumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the reported promoter pledge at 96%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge was about 5% of promoter holding given to MCX for hedging, and that the exchange data is wrong; no shares pledged to banks. It also acknowledged a small personal sale in the March quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne hold at ~₹62 per kg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 5% margin, which equals about ₹60-65 per kg at current copper prices; not expected to grow much faster than copper prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5,000 crore target purely copper, and why demerge?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the ₹5,000 crore target is for the copper company alone; non-copper revenue is under ₹10 crore. Demerger separates land and windmills from the copper business.

qa_highlights.question: Market value split between real estate and copper after demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate book value is about ₹29 crore and could be worth 10-20 times that; did not expect a market cap reduction for the copper entity.

risks_watch: Scrap supply disruption from Gulf shipping transit delays; Q1 FY27 volume may be marginally below Q4.
Demerger depends on NOCs from ROC, Regional Director, Official Liquidator and income tax authorities before NCLT hearing on 9 June.
Rising working capital (₹230 crore) and borrowings tied to copper price; interest cost could erode PAT growth relative to EBITDA.
Entry of Adani and Hindalco into recycling could increase competition and sourcing pressure.

Reporting inaccuracies on screener and exchange sites (promoter pledge shown at 96%) and a ~5% promoter-holding change management attributed to pledge versus sale; management said it has sent multiple correction letters.
Proposed fundraise of about ₹150 crore has no final structure yet.
Plastic recycling ROI and 12-15 month payback to be verified on execution.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and long-term growth, but cautious on near-term margin (targeting only ~5% and declining to predict price-driven growth). Evasive on fundraise structure, EBITDA-per-tonne peer comparisons and pledge/shareholding data, which management attributed to exchange reporting errors.
key_quotes: We are hopeful of maintaining 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year, and on an increased top line.
Our capacity has now reached 35,000 metric tonne this year, with the new, 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.
I'm not looking at it growing much faster than the copper prices.
The 5,000 crores guidance is for purely copper.

adds.what: Copper recycling capacity to 35,000 t/yr from 30,000 t (new 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad)
Heat recovery systems on furnaces to improve fuel efficiency and cut cycle times
Plastic recycling plant (cable-linked plastic to granules), ~Rs 10 cr investment, capacity reportedly 150 to 500 (unconfirmed)

growth.why: Management guides ~25% revenue growth for FY27 (about 20% volume plus 5% price) and a 5,000 cr copper-only company in ~3 years, backed by the 30,000 to 35,000 t recycling capacity increase already live, ~Rs 40 cr capex over two years and 62% value-added share, though no firm order book is cited and the Rs 150 cr fundraise is not finalised.
